migration_summary: Widen dcim_interface.speed from a 32-bit integer field to Django's PositiveBigIntegerField (bigint) so interface speeds beyond ~2.1 Gbps (e.g. 100G/400G links, expressed in Kbps) can be stored without overflow. Converted faithfully from the real Django AlterField operation to the single equivalent PostgreSQL DDL statement it generates.
migration_sql: ALTER TABLE dcim_interface ALTER COLUMN speed TYPE bigint;
schema_summary: dcim_interface is one of NetBox's largest tables in real deployments (one row per network interface across every managed device), frequently indexed and joined against for topology queries.

risk_flags.message: int4 -> int8 changes the on-disk physical width of every row's value for this column; PostgreSQL cannot do this as a metadata-only change the way some type widenings (e.g. varchar(n) -> varchar) can be, so it requires rewriting the table and rebuilding its indexes.

risk_narrative: Not every type 'widening' is equally cheap in PostgreSQL: text-length increases and some numeric-to-numeric changes with a compatible binary representation can be applied as a fast catalog-only change, but changing the integer width (int4 -> int8) changes the stored byte width and forces ACCESS EXCLUSIVE-locked table rewrite plus index rebuild. On dcim_interface specifically this matters because it is one of the largest, most-queried tables in a typical NetBox install.
lessons_learned: When predicting cost for an ALTER COLUMN TYPE, the specific source/target type pair matters more than the word 'widen' or 'narrow' — int4->int8 is a full rewrite, but some other widenings are not. Confirm via the target database's own catalog rules rather than assuming all type changes are equally cheap or equally expensive.
surprise_notes: A one-line Django AlterField (`PositiveBigIntegerField`) reads as trivial in a code review, but generates a full ACCESS EXCLUSIVE table rewrite in Postgres — the size of the diff is not a reliable signal for the size of the operation.

prediction_summary.risk_explanation: Full-table rewrite; duration and storage growth scale with dcim_interface's row count and its existing index count on the specific installation.

dimension_details.note: Real production migration from NetBox's Django migration set (netbox/dcim/migrations); migration_sql is the exact PostgreSQL DDL Django's migration executor generates for this AlterField operation, not a paraphrase.
